memory.

## Open

### F-655 — An integration run exits on CI, not on a timeout or a flag

> _2026-10-31 · realm/blong-agent · open_

An integration run does not need a timeout and does not need an exit flag: the framework already
derives it, `integration.exit` is `isCI()` in blong-gogo/src/load.ts, so
`CI=1 blong ./index.ts integration` runs the groups and returns with a status. Three runs were
wasted waiting on `timeout 150` before that was read. The same runs then exposed a second lesson
worth keeping: a column that holds JSON comes back as the text that was written or already parsed,
depending on the driver, and `String(parsed)` is `[object Object]`, which fails as a JSON syntax
error two files away from the cause. The checkpoint transcript is now read through one helper that
accepts both shapes.

### F-656 — A fixture pool without a reset lets test order decide a claim

> _2026-10-31 · realm/blong-agent · open_

Two things made the agent realm's first groups pass for the wrong reason before they passed for the
right one. A fixture pool that only hands tickets out makes every test depend on the order the
groups ran in, so a claim in one group decided what a claim in the next one got; the pool now
answers `task.pool.reset` and each group starts from its first ticket. And a session leaves behind
by a step that used another worker id is a session this host cannot suspend or answer, so a lookup
by session had to name the worker too — `agent.session.find` takes `workerId`, and the resume
precondition compares it with the host on purpose. Both were silent: the first surfaced as a missing
ticket, the second as `resumed: false` from a session that was never ours.

### F-658 — A question lost its channel at the tool boundary

> _2026-10-31 · realm/blong-agent · open_

The seam test found a chain of three things, none of which any single-realm test could see. The
agent dropped the ticket's channel at the tool boundary — `agentToolRun` called `agent.question.ask`
without `platform`/`account`/`conversationId`, so the question parked under a fallback conversation
id (`ticketId`) that no answer would ever name. Chat minted its own prompt id, so the id this realm
had already checkpointed could not be the id the answer quoted; `chat.prompt.ask` now takes an
optional `promptId` from the caller. And the checkpoint is written before the ask, so a delivery
that arrives in the microseconds between the two finds nobody parked yet — the test retries the
delivery, which is what a platform does with a retry, and the parked promise stays the authority on
which one counted. The lesson is that a cross-realm seam fails on the ids and the addressing, not on
the logic: each side was correct alone.

### F-659 — One stale suspended session without a checkpoint failed a whole suite

> _2026-10-31 · realm/blong-agent · open_

A tick that resumed every waiting answer threw agent.checkpointMissing for a row left behind by an
earlier notify run, and that single error failed the session group and every step after it, which
read as a regression from an unrelated change. A session that cannot be replayed must be skipped and
logged, and recovery purges it once it is stale, because one bad row is not a reason to stop the
loop. Clear the rows a test run leaves behind when the path under test is being changed.

### F-660 — A contributed port that the process Service already carries is a duplicate

> _2026-10-31 · realm/blong-agent · open_

Contributing k8sPorts http 8080 to make the gateway reachable produced a Service with the port
twice, because the generator appends rpc and http for every deployment and then appends the
contributed ports beside them. The gateway was reachable all along; what was missing from the run
was the kustomize realm itself, which loads only when the entry package declares
@feasibleone/blong-kustomize as a dependency. The symptoms of both were the same empty tree, so
verify the object before adding a key that names it.

### F-670 — A chat deployment started the ticket worker

> _2026-11-01 · realm/blong-agent · open_

The `slack` intent ran the agent worker, whose fixture tickets name an engine account the deployment
does not have; the tick asked a question through chat with it, the ask threw `slack.accountMissing`,
and the process died. The same worker recovery-scanned sessions left by tests and asked in their
simulated channels, which is where the `the conversation is not one the app can see` errors came
from. A conversation deployment claims no tickets, so `workerStart` is false there.

### F-671 — A colon in a prompt id broke every control that carried it

> _2026-11-01 · realm/blong-agent · open_

A platform carries a question id inside an interactive element own id, and that id is split on
colons to be read back: `chatPromptSubmit:<promptId>`. A prompt id derived from the channel as
`pick:slack:blong-bot:C0CD...` therefore shifted every field after it, so a submit arrived with the
prompt id `pick`, matched nothing parked, and was forwarded as an answer nobody waited for. The
visible symptom is that clicking does nothing and the next typed message claims the pending question
instead. Keep a prompt id free of the separator.

### F-672 — An event payload was written wider than its column

> _2026-11-01 · realm/blong-agent · open_

`agent_event.payloadJSON` is 8000 characters, and only one caller remembered to truncate: a suspend
or resume wrote a whole question or answer and the insert failed with Data too long for column
payloadJSON, taking down the run that was recording it. A trace field has one writer boundary, so
the truncation belongs in `agentEventAdd` where no caller can forget it.

### F-778 — the tap gate ran no group, so a ticket test rotted unseen

> _2026-11-20 · realm/blong-agent · open_

The tap gate for `realm/blong-agent` ran no test group at all: `index.test.ts` booted the platform,
asserted two methods were attached, and stopped. The realm's groups lived only in
`integration.watch.test`, which a `blong ./index.ts` run reads and a tap entry does not, so every
group was executed by a CLI run and by nothing in CI. A ticket test drifted with the stack: it
matched `/workspace/` against `failure.code ?? failure.message`, and over a dispatch only the
rendered message survives, where the word carries a capital — green in the one place nothing ran,
red the first time a `blong ./index.ts dev integration` run executed it. The lesson is that a gate
which asserts a realm _boots_ is not a gate over the realm: wire `platform.test(undefined)` in the
entry so the same list a deployment runs is the one the report covers.

### F-828 — The documented account check had no route behind it and a payload flag the CLI never parses

> _2026-11-24 · realm/blong-agent · open_

`blong-dev call engine.account.check --account srv1` was the documented way to prove a runtime, and
it could not work three ways at once. The method is an engine-adapter handler with no gateway
validation file, so no gateway served it and a plain call answered `Not Found`; `--account` is not a
payload flag the command parses (only `--payload.<path>` is), so the payload would have been empty;
and with no `route` entry and no `--target` the call fell back to the only server the repository's
`.blong_callrc` declares, a deployment that answered `gateway.mleUndecoded` — the MLE hook refusing
an encrypted body on a path that does not decode MLE, which includes the not-found route and reads
as a cipher problem rather than a missing route. The route now exists in
`gateway/engine/engine.account.check.ts`. The lesson is that a documented `blong-dev call` line
needs a route behind it and the payload spelling the CLI actually reads.

### F-837 — A snapshot inside the pixel budget is never rewritten, even with --update-snapshots

> _2026-11-24 · realm/blong-agent · open_

The transcript picture kept showing numbers from a build that had already changed: the page rendered
`800 ms` while the committed PNG still said `300 ms`, and `blong-dev playwright --update-snapshots`
reported `1 passed` without rewriting the file. The cause is
`expect.toHaveScreenshot.maxDiffPixelRatio: 0.001` in the core Playwright config — a changed digit
in a 1280×1600 picture is a few hundred pixels, well inside the budget, so Playwright judges the
snapshot current and `--update-snapshots` (mode `changed`) writes nothing. The flag has to be
`--update-snapshots=all` to rewrite unconditionally, and `npx playwright test` reaches it directly
while the dev CLI's own flag did not. The lesson: when a snapshot is meant to change and the run
says it passed, check the file's mtime before believing the run, and never debug the page for a
value the picture is not reading.

### F-838 — A pattern subpath in a package's exports map does not resolve under the tap loader

> _2026-11-25 · realm/blong-agent · open_

`import bash from '@speed-highlight/core/languages/bash.js'` resolves under plain node and under
Vite, and under tap it fails with `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED` naming `./languages/bash.js`,
because the package's exports key is the pattern `./languages/*.js` while the index `./languages` is
a literal key and resolves fine. The unit suite is the gate, so the per-language imports — the thing
that keeps a bundle to the grammars it uses — had to be replaced by the whole registry. The lesson:
before designing around a package's granular subpath exports, put one such import in a tap test file
and run it; a literal subpath resolving is not evidence that a pattern subpath will, and the failure
appears only in the suite, after the browser build has already worked.

### F-843 — blong ./index.ts dev never finishes starting, so a manual run is the playwright intent set

> _2026-11-25 · realm/blong-agent · open_

`blong ./index.ts dev` — the command the skill calls the developer loop, and the port
`.blong_callrc` names for `local` — never finishes starting on this machine: the log stops after
every port's `adapter.ready` and nothing listens, which reads as a hang rather than as a refusal.

Two things were learned finding the run that does work. The intent list decides the rc file by its
LAST name, so `dev microservice` reads `.blong_microservicerc` (absent) and silently loses the dev
rc — `dev` has to be last, or `--config` names the file. And starting is what `integration` fixes:
it sets `canSkipSocket`, so a call resolves in-process instead of dialling a service name; without
it the run either stalls at the post-ready steps or, with `--resolution=false`, dies on `EAI_AGAIN`
for `rpc-core`.

The recipe that listens, keeps the dev rc's engine accounts and streams into the page runs
`blong-watch microservice integration dev --config .blong_devrc` with `--gateway.port=8080` and
`--resolution.portGateway=8080`. The browser runner's own list adds `playwright`, which is what a
spec wants and what a watched run should leave out: it switches the feed to the in-memory ring, so a
run somebody is observing publishes nowhere. Until `dev` alone is repaired, that is what a manual
run is, and `scripts/runTask.sh` and the session pattern doc both say so.

## Resolved

### F-651 — A base adapter that skips super.connect leaves start pending

> _2026-10-31 · realm/blong-agent · resolved_

A base adapter that never calls super.connect() leaves its port queue without a loop, and the
platform's start then waits for a promise that never settles: the log still shows adapter.start and
adapter.ready, the listeners come up, and a tap test expires at thirty seconds with two server
handles open. This is what the first version of adapter.agent did, and the fixture task adapter
looked like the culprit only because it was the other base-less file in the tree; extending
adapter.http fixed it by accident, since http calls super.connect(). The fix in
core/blong-gogo/src/adapter/server/agent.ts is a start() that calls super.connect() before
super.start().

adapter.agent now connects in start(); the realm boots with agent.task and agent.engine attached

### F-653 — An upgrade built a gateway, and the gateway dialled every model

> _2026-10-31 · realm/blong-agent · resolved_

A bare `blong ./index.ts upgrade` in the agent realm ended with RequestError getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN
rpc-core on http://rpc-core:8091/rpc/ports/core/request and left agent_answer uncreated. The schema
was never the problem: `core/blong-server/orchestrator/subject/validation.ts` builds the gateway
validations for every `public: true` model and reads each spec with `handler[handlerName]({}, {})`,
a call through the handler proxy that names another namespace (`core.label.model`,
`core.translation.model`, `access.access.model`). The upgrade intent in `blong-gogo/src/load.ts` was
`{exit: true}` alone, so a migration run still built a gateway, and the gateway is what asks for
those validations — with no server started there was nothing to answer the call and the host stayed
a bare `rpc-core`. The first fix, `remote.canSkipSocket` in the realm's own upgrade block, worked
but answered the wrong question: the realm was buying in-process dispatch to make a step run that an
upgrade has no business running. The block now turns the serving components off — gateway,
rpcServer, apiGateway, restFs, systemDebug, mcp — the same set `cli` and `k8s` turn off (`D-713`),
and the realm flag is gone. Verified with the flag removed: the upgrade exits 0, no request leaves
the process, and all four tables exist.

### F-654 — An orchestrator cannot inject its persistence handlers by name

> _2026-10-31 · realm/blong-agent · resolved_

Group 6's first group, test.agent.session, is wired and runs against the integration intent, but
every step that reaches persistence fails with Handler 'agentAnswerFind' not found. The call is made
from an orchestrator handler through its injected handler proxy, and that proxy only knows the
caller's own folder (F-641); a probe step calling agentSessionFind from the test layer passes, so
the handlers are registered and the fault is the scope, not the registry. Adding `db` to the
orchestrator's imports made the names resolve and every call throw Database not available, because
the handlers then ran on the orchestrator's port and this.config.context.queryBuilder belongs to the
db adapter's instance; that is reverted. The fix is to call persistence through the port the handler
answers on, which the dispatch already routes to destination db: a small db(method, params, $meta)
helper over port.dispatch, and every injected persistence name replaced with its dotted wire name
(agent.session.get, agent.checkpoint.add, agent.answer.find, ...). Separately,
orchestrator/session/agentTools.ts is refused by the watcher as a generic source file in a handler
group folder; it needs to be a library() injected into agentToolRun.

Fixed with the documented shape: only the adapter whose namespace differs from the method needs the
prefix, so db/agentSessionAdd resolves while taskNextTask stays bare; two of the three test steps
now pass.

### F-783 — A ledger assertion matched by recency, and compared the runner's name

> _2026-11-20 · realm/blong-agent · resolved_

The reach test looked for the flow ledger execution that carries agentTicketClaimed by taking the
first match, and the list is ordered by which execution was touched last. Every group in the package
runs a tick, so several executions carry that signal: locally the session group's tick was touched
last and the assertion passed, in CI the recovery group's was and it failed with expected
agent.worker.tick, actual test.agent.recovery.

The deeper mistake was the field it compared. A flow's kind is the name of the group the runner
opened - test.agent.session, test.agent.recovery - while the tick is the leg inside it, which is
what the diagram is drawn from and what is the same in every group. So the test now finds the
execution by the flow id its own record carries, and asserts the leg it was announced under rather
than the kind of whoever ran it. A list read by recency is a list to match by identity, and a
runner's name is not the realm's.

Fixed in test/lukaot.reach.test.ts: the execution is found by the flow id the claim record carries,
and the assertion is on the agent.worker.tick leg — the same in every group — rather than on the
kind, which is the runner's group name. Verified by three consecutive green runs of the package
(53/53).

### F-822 — The copilot intent's ad-hoc account was named local and shadowed the integration sim account

> _2026-11-23 · realm/blong-agent · resolved_

A verification run with the new intent left eight tests red. The `copilot` block added an account
called `local` for a runtime started by hand, and `config.integration` claims with an account of the
same name whose script the session group depends on. The accounts are one merged map across every
intent of an instance, so the later block replaced the scripted account and the group
dialled 127.0.0.1:4321 instead of replaying a script. The account is now `laptop`, and the lesson is
that an alias is a key shared by every intent, so a new intent must never reuse one. A run of the
suite with the intent's own accounts is what catches it; the integration run without the intent
cannot.

The account is now laptop across adapter/engine.ts, the README and the plan's sample; a run
with --intent copilot passes 25/25 where it failed 8 before.

### F-836 — A gateway route is not a method the page can call

> _2026-11-24 · realm/blong-agent · resolved_

`Portal.call` runs `window.__blongHandler[name]`, and that proxy binds the namespaces the _browser_
loads, not the routes the gateway serves. `test.run.start` is a gateway validation in
`realm/blong-test/gateway/test/`, so it is reachable over HTTP and invisible in the page; the first
attempt at seeding a browser spec through it failed with `remote.bindingFailed` and read like a
broken test realm. The same rule in the other direction is what made the fix cheap: a server `test`
group listed in the intent's `watch.test` runs at boot, through the watcher every integration run
already uses, and the spec then opens the page and reads what the server wrote. Lesson: to seed a
page, use what the run already does at startup, or a method the page's own namespaces carry; a
gateway route is not one.

Resolved by doing the opposite: the seeding is a server test group that the playwright intent's
watcher runs at boot, so the spec calls nothing to seed and the page needs no test surface.

### F-833 — agent.* is claimed by the db port, so a dispatched method must live in its group

> _2026-11-24 · realm/blong-agent · resolved_

A handler in `adapter/telemetry/` was never reached by name: the shared `srv.db` adapter claims
`agent.*` (its namespace), so `remote.dispatch('agent.telemetry.insert')` found the db port first
and the db exec built an insert into a table named after the method (`agent_telemetry` did not
exist). Moving the file to `orchestrator/telemetry/` did not help; placing it in `adapter/db/` — the
group whose handlers the db port imports — did, because that port answers by handler name before
falling through to `exec`. So a dispatched method must live in the group that serves the realm's
namespace, not merely in the realm, and a `Lib property ... not found` error afterwards proved a
second rule: an injected library function belongs to the group that declares it, so a handler in
another group imports it directly. Both cost a full restart-and-read cycle each, which is why they
are written down.

The constraint was real but the shape it forced was wrong: the dispatch forwards a method it does
not answer itself, so a handler the orchestrator defines answers before the forward happens. The two
handlers that were written in the db group to satisfy it are orchestrations and now live in
orchestrator/session/, calling their adapters with qualified names — wire names, frames and stored
documents unchanged, verified by the realm's tap suite, the integration run against Kafka and the
Playwright spec (D-1013).

### F-842 — A failing session step reproduces at HEAD, so it is the dev database and not the change

> _2026-11-25 · realm/blong-agent · resolved_

While verifying the wake move, `aStoredAnswerIsResumedByTheNextTick` failed in three consecutive
session-group runs, and the first suspicion was the change: the tick had claimed a second ticket
instead of resuming the parked session, so `next.resumed` was zero. The failure reproduces with the
task's own files stashed (`git stash push -m "T-816 wip" -- <the six touched files>`), so it belongs
to the machine's accumulated state rather than to the change — the dev database carried 375 claimed,
103 running and 41 failed sessions from earlier runs and aborted notify runs, and the pool's tickets
behave differently depending on which row a claim reaches. The lesson is the cheap check that
settled it: before debugging a failure into a change, run the same group with exactly the touched
files stashed, because a scoped stash costs a minute and a wrong diagnosis costs an hour. It also
means this step is a real fragility of the group — it depends on the first tick's session still
being resumable when the step suspends it — and the durable fix is for the step to assert the
suspended status before it adds the answer, naming which half broke.

The step suspends the session the tick it just ran opened, so the resume it asserts is the same
session: both boots of the realm's groups ran it green on the accumulated dev database, twice in one
log, alongside sixteen other steps with no failure. The fragility is not reproducible now; the
lesson the entry records — stash exactly the touched files before blaming a change — stays with it.

### F-844 — The session page was invisible because the capability map omits its own reads

> _2026-11-25 · realm/blong-agent · resolved_

The session page could not be opened by any shipped role: `meta/db/accessAuthorizationMerge.yaml`
granted `agentSessionGet` and the write actions but not `agentSessionFind` or `agentSessionWatch`,
so the portal's own menu filter — which hides an entry whose `permission` the session does not hold
— dropped the Agent group entirely, and the page was unreachable with nothing failing anywhere. The
Playwright spec never saw it because its fixture grants every page (`blongPermissions: true`), so a
test that reads the page cannot notice a missing grant. Two facts made it look like a frontend bug
instead of a seed: the merged portal config still contained the group (the filter is applied at
render, not at merge), and `agent.session.find` answered over the gateway because a `blong-dev call`
token carries capabilities the browser's menu does not read the same way. Adding both reads to
`agentManage`, `agentMaintain` and `agentView` and restarting the backend is what fixed it — a YAML
edit alone does not, because the running process holds the map it built at boot.

The capability map grants agentSessionFind and agentSessionWatch to agentManage, agentMaintain and
agentView (meta/db/accessAuthorizationMerge.yaml), and the portal's Agent group has been open in
every session since. What the entry records stays the part that mattered: the Playwright fixture
grants every page, so a spec cannot notice a missing grant, and a YAML edit needs the process
restarted because it builds the map at boot.

### F-846 — A long native task dies at 60 seconds because the SDK waits that long for session.idle

> _2026-11-25 · realm/blong-agent · resolved_

The first UI tour run (session 601c2578) aborted with
`Timeout after 60000ms waiting for session.idle` after seven tools and 45 s of work, and the run
looked like a model that gave up. The copilot SDK waits 60 s for `session.idle` by default, so any
task whose steps sleep or run a slow command is cut off however long the realm allows.
`timeoutMs: 600000` on the account in `.blong_devrc` is what fixes it, and the account is the right
home because the wait belongs to the runtime connection rather than to the run, and a second connect
clamp of 10 s sits in the same place.

Both accounts in .blong_devrc carry timeoutMs: 600000, and every run since has outlived the old
ceiling — the last two finished at 120 s and 90 s of tool time with no idle timeout. The entry keeps
the reason it belongs on the account: the wait is the runtime connection's, not the run's.

### F-847 — A local dispatch answers with a pair, and nothing said so: a question's answer arrived as ok true

> _2026-11-25 · realm/blong-agent · resolved_

A native run asked a person a question and the model was told `{"ok": true}`. The realm was right
the whole time — the checkpoint held the question and the echo had answered in 84 ms — and three
readings of the code found nothing, because `api.remote.dispatch` answers a local request with the
pair the framework packs a decoded result into, `[payload, {mtid: "response"}]`, while the engine
read `result` off it and fell back to its own acknowledgement. What settled it was three lines of
logging around the call: the pair was in the log on the first run. The lesson is to print the value
a boundary returns before reasoning about it, and the fix is one exported helper,
`engineDispatchResult`.

engineDispatchResult unpacks the framework pair in the engine adapter, and the runtime's tool call
id now travels into agent.tool.run, so the checkpoint names the pending call. Five assertions pin
the unwrap, two pin the bridge, and a live run shows the model reading the person's answer.

### F-848 — A page module that gains an import needs a hard reload, or the browser reports the name as undefined

> _2026-11-25 · realm/blong-agent · resolved_

Twice in one session the page failed with `sessionEventsMerge is not defined` and
`wrappedOf is not defined` after a sibling module gained a helper: Vite hot-updated the importing
module and kept the cached copy of the imported one, so the new name resolved to nothing and React
dropped the tree into its error boundary. Neither failure was a code fault — a reload with a
cache-busting query fixed both — and each one read like a real defect for a minute. When a change
adds a name across two modules of the page, reload before judging the error.

Nothing in the code can prevent it: Vite updates the importing module and keeps the cached copy of
the one that gained a name. The entry keeps the workaround it cost a minute to learn — reload with a
cache-busting query before judging such an error — and the page no longer fails this way in a normal
run.

### F-845 — The session page spec takes the newest row, so a manual run's feed sessions displace its seed

> _2026-11-25 · realm/blong-agent · resolved_

`test/agentSession.play.ts` opened with `list.locator('tr[data-session]').first()` and expected it
to be the session `test.agent.ui` seeded at boot, which holds only while nothing writes a newer one.
A manual run starts the same intent set the runner does — `microservice integration dev playwright`
— so the integration groups' feed test writes its own sessions a moment after the seed, and the spec
then read `feed-oldest` instead and failed on `toContainText('Render the session')` before it took a
screenshot. It is the same class as F-842: a spec that depends on the database's newest row rather
than on its own fixture. The fix is to find the seeded row by what the seed wrote (its title, or the
id the seeding group returns) instead of by position; until then the spec passes only where the
database is fresh, which is why CI is green and a developer's machine is not.

The spec finds its row by the title the seed writes — `Render the session` — instead of by position,
so a newer session from any other run no longer shadows it. The deeper half turned out to be the run
rather than the row: Playwright reuses a server already on the backend port, and a dev backend
without the `playwright` intent seeds nothing, which is recorded and closed as T-826. The suite is
green on its own ports.
